score_rationale: Strong willingness-to-pay validated by active commercial market: at least 6 major vendors (BizProspex, ContactOut, ReadyContacts, eSalesClub, DataCaptive, AverickMedia) currently selling architect databases ranging from 15K to 1.3M+ records (note: higher counts likely include non-licensed design professionals) with pricing from $200 baseline for verified architect lists. Five high-value B2B buyer segments: (1) architecture software vendors (Autodesk AEC Collection including Revit, SketchUp, Bentley MicroStation, Graphisoft ArchiCAD, Vectorworks Architect) selling BIM/CAD design platforms, rendering tools, and building information modeling software at $2,500-$7,000/year per seat — architecture software vendors pay $8,000-$20,000/year for targeted architect marketing lists to acquire customers with $5,000-$20,000/year LTV; (2) AIA continuing education providers and AIA-approved CE course vendors (AIAU, Architectural Record CEU, Building Design+Construction, RedVector, PDH Academy) selling mandatory learning units — all licensed architects must complete continuing education (varies by state: California requires 5 AIA LUs annually, New York requires 36 hours triennially, Texas requires 12 hours annually, Florida requires 20 hours biennially) to maintain license renewal, creating recurring $150-$500/year spend per architect on AIA-approved courses; (3) professional liability insurance carriers (The Hartford, CNA, XL Catlin, Victor Insurance, JAUNICH) selling errors and omissions coverage required by AIA contracts and most architecture firm employment — premiums range $3,000-$15,000/year per architect depending on project types (residential vs. commercial high-rise), project values, firm size, claims history, and coverage limits ($1M/$2M typical, higher for large projects); (4) building product manufacturers and architectural specification vendors (windows, doors, HVAC systems, lighting, roofing, cladding, flooring) targeting architects for product specifications and inclusion in project drawings — manufacturers pay $5,000-$15,000/year for architect databases to market specification-grade products that architects write into construction documents and project specs; and (5) architecture recruitment firms and design talent agencies placing architects in firm roles, in-house corporate positions, and government agency jobs with placements generating $12,000-$35,000 in fees per hire at typical $80K-$140K salary levels. All 55 U.S. jurisdictions (50 states + DC + Guam + Northern Mariana Islands + Puerto Rico + US Virgin Islands) maintain public architect license rosters via their State Architectural Registration Boards or Department of Professional Regulation, accessible through NCARB (National Council of Architectural Registration Boards) centralized lookup tool and state-specific websites with no authentication required. Data includes architect full name, license number, license status (active, inactive, retired, suspended, revoked), initial licensure date, firm affiliation (where disclosed), practice address (availability varies by state), and disciplinary history (public actions only). Zero PII — all professional credential and disciplinary data under state architecture practice acts and freedom of information laws. Engineering lift is moderate: scrape or download from 55 state architectural boards (California CAB, New York SED, Texas TBAE, Florida DBPR all confirmed publicly searchable), deduplicate multi-jurisdiction architects (many hold reciprocal licenses via NCARB Certificate for multi-state practice), normalize status codes and practice specialties, flag disciplinary records. No affordable flat-file competitor exists on Gumroad or similar marketplaces — all existing vendors sell annual subscriptions ($4,000-$12,000/year) or per-record pricing ($0.25-$0.60/record), leaving a clear gap for a one-time $129-$149 CSV. Audience size is substantial: approximately 120,000 licensed architects nationwide (113,554 NCARB-certificated architects as of 2024 plus additional state-only licenses), creating a TAM of 4,000+ potential B2B buyers across architecture software, AIA CE providers, insurance, building products, and recruiting verticals. Score is 8 due to validated high willingness-to-pay from multiple commercial vendors at premium pricing ($200+ baseline), confirmed public data availability across all 55 jurisdictions with NCARB centralized lookup and state board aggregation, absence of low-cost flat-file alternatives, substantial architect population (120K), and five distinct B2B buyer segments with proven high-LTV purchasing behavior in architecture software, insurance, and building products markets.

data_wanted: All 55 U.S. jurisdictions (50 states + DC + Guam + Northern Mariana Islands + Puerto Rico + US Virgin Islands) maintain public architect license rosters via their State Architectural Registration Boards or Department of Professional Regulation, accessible through NCARB (National Council of Architectural Registration Boards) centralized architect lookup tool at ncarb.org/get-licensed/state-licensing-boards/architect-lookup and state-specific board websites with no authentication required for lookup. California Architects Board (CAB at cab.ca.gov), New York State Education Department (SED), Texas Board of Architectural Examiners (TBAE at tbae.texas.gov), Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation (DBPR), and 51 additional state architectural boards all provide public searchable databases. NCARB maintains a national directory linking to all 55 member board license verification portals. Key fields per license: architect full name (first, middle initial, last), state license number (format varies by state, typically alphanumeric 4-8 characters), initial licensure date (date of first architect license issuance in that state), license expiration/renewal date (where publicly listed — some states show next renewal date, others do not disclose), license status (active, inactive, retired, delinquent, suspended, revoked), NCARB Certificate number and status (where applicable — indicates architect has NCARB Certificate enabling reciprocal licensure across states via streamlined process), firm affiliation or practice name (where voluntarily disclosed or required by state), practice address (street, city, state, ZIP — availability varies significantly by state based on public records policies; some states list full business address, others only city/state, some redact entirely per architect privacy election), disciplinary history (public disciplinary actions, suspensions, and revocations — private warnings or reprimands not included), and areas of specialization or practice focus (where voluntarily disclosed). Target all active and inactive licenses (exclude only revoked or permanently surrendered). Scope to individual architects only — exclude architecture firms or unlicensed design professionals. Approximately 120,000 architect licenses nationwide as of 2026 (113,554 NCARB Certificate holders as of NCARB 2024 annual report + additional state-only licenses estimated 5,000-8,000). Target output: 120K rows, one per license (some individuals appear multiple times if licensed in multiple states via reciprocity). Data is 100% public per state architecture practice acts and state Freedom of Information laws — architect licensing and disciplinary records are public information under NCARB Model Law and state professional practice statutes.
